MCP error messages daily draft (2026-09-30) — teach-first + paper fact

Status: CEO PASS (teach-first + paper fact). Show Ashish for cut. Do not post. Owner publishes.

Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35381

Figures: /workspace/article/harness-research/2026-09-30-mcp-figures/ (Table 3 + Table 4)

Patches:

  1. Scene + verbatim “Please run: reddit-mcp-buddy --auth.” + Astra 6% vs 75% before methods.
  2. Exact 82% for strip and cause-alone; no second “raised to 84%”.

An agent’s login has expired. The tool fails. The error says: “Please run: reddit-mcp-buddy --auth.”

That means: open a terminal and run a login command. The agent has no terminal. It can only call the tools the server already listed. It tries to follow the line anyway, then gives up.

On GPT-6 Astra that path recovered 6%; with the terminal command removed, 75%. Same login-expired failure. Same tools. A 69 point drop.

Xu and Wu kept the agents, tools, and saved state fixed and changed only that next-step sentence. Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers wrap outside tools (login, tickets, GitHub) and hand the model these error strings. Recovery means the turn finishes the real job after the failure.

Original step: 45%. Name a server tool: 84%.

Mean of five OpenAI models. The named-tool form was “Call ticket_login first.” Strip the unreachable terminal line before the model sees it, and you get 82%. Cause alone, with no tool named, also lands at 82%.

Stronger models follow tool-output instructions more reliably. Here the instruction is written for a developer sitting at a keyboard, not for an agent that can only call tools.

What I still want measured is how often live servers ship the “call this tool” form versus the “run this in a terminal” form after this paper lands.

If you ship these errors: name a tool the agent can call, or strip the unreachable step before the model sees it.
